axes.label: Government / sovereign-cloud price premium
axes.question: Does the authorized-region premium explain why this load is sited here?
drives: the authorized-region-premium driver in the end-use / who-captures-the-benefit analysis
axes.basis: The recurring price premium government/sovereign cloud commands over commercial (isolation, U.S.-persons staffing, compliance) is what would reward building dedicated hardened capacity in a low-cost jurisdiction. That the premium exists is documented; that it applies to this campus is not — the facility's authorization posture is undisclosed (docs/defense-nexus.md). ~20-30% recurring premium (isolation, U.S.-persons staffing, compliance). Already multi-sourced in the relator's data appendix (BCG, AWS GovCloud vs commercial, CapLinked, Matlock); carried here so the prior has one home. Application to Lima [open].

axes.label: AI hardware refresh cycle and rack power density
axes.question: Does AI-class hardware break the equipment forecast the DCTE was scored against?
axes.basis: Ohio's data-center sales-tax exemption is scored against a single equipment-purchase forecast. AI-class hardware refreshes on a 3-5 year cycle at ~30-40% of hardware cost annually, and rack density is rising, so the exempted base recurs across the abatement window rather than being spent once. Whether this campus takes the exemption, and on how much hardware, is not in the record. AI-class hardware refreshes on a 3-5 yr cycle (~30-40% of hardware cost annually in opex); rack power density jumps 5-15 kW (enterprise) to 120-140 kW (GB200), projected 250-900 kW/rack by 2027. Drives the RECURRENCE of the DCTE sales-tax exemption — the exemption is scored against a single equipment forecast that AI refresh breaks.

axes.label: Building (abated real-property) share of total capex
axes.question: How much of the build is abated real property rather than exempt equipment?
drives: the CRA 75%/15-yr property-tax abatement base (the abated assessed value)
axes.basis: The CRA abates real property only; the DCTE covers equipment and construction materials. The split is jurisdiction-specific and genuinely fuzzy, and it is the single knob that moves the most money between the two subsidies. Independent capex breakdowns put the building SHELL at ~15-21% of total cost; with affixed mechanical/electrical fixtures classified as real property the abated base rises toward ~40-50%. Ohio's CRA abates REAL property; the DCTE sales-tax exemption covers equipment AND construction materials (R.C. 122.175) — so the building/equipment line is genuinely fuzzy and jurisdiction-specific, which is exactly why this is a band. The corpus's earlier single 0.35 sits inside it.

axes.label: Steady-state permanent jobs per MW (automated hyperscale)
axes.question: How many permanent jobs does a load this size actually carry?
drives: the job-count input to the per-job and load-not-jobs figures
axes.basis: Automated hyperscale campuses run roughly 20-40 operators per 100 MW. Applied to a load of this scale the range independently brackets the agreement's own non-binding estimate, which is why the job count is turned across a band rather than taken at its stated value. Automated hyperscale campuses run ~20-40 operators per 100 MW (0.2-0.3/MW); the most automated sites approach 0.1/MW. For Lima's ~275-348 MW that is ~28-105 jobs — which independently brackets the CRA's non-binding ~50 (mid-low) and the leaner 30-job profile. Colocation runs higher per MW; bitcoin near zero.

axes.label: Subsidy per data-center job (comparative benchmark)
axes.question: Is the modeled subsidy per job typical of a data-center deal, or an outlier?
drives: a sanity band the ledger's modeled per-job subsidy is read against
axes.basis: A comparative benchmark the modeled per-job figures are read against — a corroboration of the output, never an input to it. Good Jobs First: data-center megadeals average ~$2M/job (Illinois ~$1.4M; North Carolina/Apple ~$6.4M; Digital Realty >$2M). BOSC's modeled property-tax abatement alone is ~$0.6-2.1M/job; adding the sales-tax exemption puts the total squarely in this band — i.e. TYPICAL of a data-center megadeal, not an outlier. A corroboration of the ledger output, not an input.

axes.label: The sales-tax exemption is the dominant data-center subsidy
axes.question: Which subsidy is actually the larger one?
axes.basis: Every jurisdiction that has measured it reports the sales-tax exemption, not the property abatement, as the dominant cost. A qualitative corroboration from other states — it asserts no magnitude here, which is why it carries no band. Corroborates the ledger's "second subsidy no one scores." Virginia's JLARC found the data-center sales-and-use exemption cost $1.02B in FY2024 — 81% of ALL state incentive spending. Ohio's own DCTE ballooned to ~$16B, prompting a 2025-26 move to suspend new grants (HB957). The exemption — not the property abatement — is repeatedly the largest line, at the scale of states that have actually measured it.

load_per_job.note: IT load 250-300 MW (OEPA Air PTI P0138965 (Facility 0302022054), committed data/extracted/permits/4132514.epa.yaml (final, 2026-05-28): 114 hall gensets x 2.75 MW (~2,750 ekW) = ~313 MW backup; IT ~250-300 MW (N+1). Per-engine rating from the draft public notice (3987141/3987144); engine size CBI-redacted in the final permit under an Ohio EPA trade-secret grant (OAC 3745-49-03, 2025-10-08; data/extracted/permits/3859883.epa.yaml).) over 30-50 modeled jobs. The central is the reference corner — the load at the agreement's own stated headcount. This is the magnitude behind the structural reading that the public instrument is scaled to load and consumption rather than to employment; it is a ratio of two modeled quantities, not a finding about intent.

method: 15-yr forgone real-property tax = capex x building_share x assessment_ratio x effective_commercial_mills x abatement_percent x term_years; forgone sales tax (the DCTE, if taken) = (1 - building_share) x capex x sales_and_use_rate x equipment_refresh; net subsidy = the two, before the withheld school-compensation offset. Each is priced at every scenario corner and published as the envelope of those corners.
disclaimer: A labeled counterfactual, not a finding. Every figure here is a band across explicitly stated scenarios whose constants are all on the table — it prices what the public instrument WOULD cost under each set of assumptions, and asserts nothing about which one is true. The GovCloud / defense-hardened profile in particular is a what-if on two knobs (building share and headcount); it is NOT a claim that this facility does defense work. That question is open and the corpus does not answer it (docs/defense-nexus.md).
caveats: Every figure here is a band across labeled scenarios, not an estimate of what will happen. The constants are all published above; turn any of them and the band moves.
The effective commercial millage is a STATED ASSUMPTION, not a cited Allen County, OH rate — it scales every dollar figure linearly and is the largest unforced uncertainty in the model.
The abatement is on real property only, so the building/equipment split moves money between the two subsidies rather than shrinking the total.
The sales-tax exemption line is conditional: whether this campus holds a DCTE agreement is not in the record.
The school-compensation offset is a wide screening range because the agreement's dollar terms are non-public — the net-subsidy line is stated before it, not net of it.
The single figure that would most narrow this band — the School District Compensation Agreement — is withheld by the county, which is why the band is wide.
